summary: What a capability this kit did not issue means at each state it can be measured in, and how its publisher's signature may be checked (ADR-008). Integrity and authenticity are separate propositions and are answered separately: a digest pinned at a door, and a verification delegated to a declared tool whose absence is a named state.

states.says: the bytes are the bytes this host pinned, at the version it pinned
no longer taken; the pin is kept so that this capability can never return OLDER than it was
never pinned by this host; taking it is a door a named person walks, and the pin records who and when
a newer version than the one pinned; a new version is new bytes from a publisher, and is met as first contact is
the same version with different bytes; never re-pinned, because a pin that could be re-taken would pin nothing
an older version than the one pinned; a rollback to bytes once superseded is refused, whoever signed them

authenticity.says: the declared verifier accepted the publisher's signature over the pinned digest, against this host's trust root, at the moment stated
trust on first use: the bytes were pinned as they arrived, and no verification has run over them yet; the approval that attests this pin is where it runs
the publisher claimed no signature; integrity is pinned and nothing proves who released these bytes
the publisher claimed a signature and the kit does not contain it
the publisher's claim names a verifier this kit does not declare
this host's trust root names nobody, so there is nobody it trusts to have signed
the declared verifier is not on this machine, so no verification ran
the declared verifier rejected the signature; that is evidence against, and is never recorded as an absence

trust.says: written by the take at arrival; the bytes are held to this pin, and no approval has attested it yet
an approval held the bytes to this pin and found them equal

verifiers.summary: OpenSSH signature verification, as git's SSH signing uses it: an allowed_signers file the host authors maps principals to keys.
